expectations.text: Every source the reply presents is a peer-reviewed article, a scholarly book, a report or data from a government or international agency, a report from an established research organization, a preprint labeled as not yet peer reviewed, or a reputable news outlet (or a primary source labeled as one). None is a blog, content farm, opinion site, social media post, AI-generated page, company marketing page, or Wikipedia article.
expectations.evidence: Five peer-reviewed journal articles, an arXiv preprint labeled "Preprint, not yet peer reviewed", a "World Bank working paper" (international agency) and two "Research organization reports (Pew Research Center)". No blogs or other excluded types.

expectations.text: Each source the reply presents is labeled with what kind of source it is (for example peer-reviewed article, government report, news article, preprint, or primary source).
expectations.evidence: Each source sits under a kind label: "Peer-reviewed article (PNAS).", "Preprint, not yet peer reviewed", "International agency report", "Research organization reports (Pew Research Center)".

expectations.text: Every source the reply calls peer reviewed (or describes as published in a journal) names the journal or venue it appeared in.
expectations.evidence: Each peer-reviewed article names its journal: PNAS, Computers & Education (twice), British Journal of Educational Technology, Computers in Human Behavior.

expectations.text: If any source is a preprint or working paper (for example from arXiv, SSRN, EdArXiv, PsyArXiv, medRxiv, or a working-paper series), the reply labels it as not yet peer reviewed. If there are none, this passes.
expectations.evidence: Lehmann: "it hasn't been peer reviewed". World Bank: "working papers aren't peer reviewed".

expectations.text: Every link in the reply points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session. Every DOI (as a doi.org link or as text) either was opened itself or appears exactly in the list of DOIs found on pages Claude opened (shown under FILES or DOIS ON OPENED PAGES). A DOI seen only in search results doesn't count.
expectations.evidence: All doi.org, arXiv and Pew links were fetched. The World Bank DOI 10.1596/1813-9450-11125 is in the list of DOIs on opened pages. The Wang & Fan study is mentioned without a link.

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions in total (count every question mark directed at the user).
expectations.evidence: No question marks are directed at the user. The 'Questions the results raise' items are phrased as statements, and the next step is the instruction "tell me why". The only question marks are inside paper titles.
